items.assumption: FRANK loop/readout/state numerics can participate in semantic identity and deterministic replay.
items.ancestry: FRANK loop-of-loops directive plus ClayCode/Harness shared architecture lineage
items.independent_discriminator: Local Python-vs-Node raw-bit numeric serialization experiment plus primary language/canonicalization/runtime specifications.
items.result: Numeric identity is feasible only with an explicit typed canonicalization/lowering contract; host presentation is insufficient.
items.falsifier: Production canonicalizer proves equivalent semantics without such explicit rules.

items.assumption: Typed canonicalization is sufficient for exact Int lowering to every host numeric type.
items.result: Lowering must prove target-range exactness or use an exact representation; semantic token stability alone does not protect execution values.

items.assumption: A single generic NaN/Infinity policy can be promoted immediately.
items.result: The representation mismatch is real, but executable-domain policy depends on whether special values/payload identity are admitted and observable. Production compiler/backend tests are required.

items.assumption: Numeric readouts, graph weights, GWT scores or loop metrics can authorize effects after canonicalization.
items.result: Canonicalization changes representation identity only. Model output, activation, readout or numeric score remains non-authoritative without the external capability/commit path.

items.assumption: FRANK requires new numeric-specific ClayCode syntax to resolve the observed issue.
items.result: No executable evidence requires new syntax. Existing typed semantic IR plus checker/canonicalizer/lowering contracts is the lower-complexity candidate.

anti_echo_boundary: FRANK/ClayCode/Harness agreement is not counted as independent replication; only the new executable differential and external primary specifications add independent discrimination.
